question: What is the maximum dilutive impact in number of shares of Snapchat's outstanding convertible notes as of 12/31/2024?
answer: 85,945,127 shares if all converts were converted (including out of the money converts)

model_answer:
## Answer

**≈ 85.9 million shares (85,945 thousand)** — that is the maximum share dilution from Snap’s convertible notes outstanding at 12/31/2024, computed on the if-converted basis (i.e., presuming every note is settled entirely in Class A shares at its stated conversion rate).

Snap’s FY2024 Form 10-K (filed Feb 5, 2025), in the “Net loss per share” note, reports the potentially dilutive shares excluded as anti-dilutive:

| Anti-dilutive securities (in thousands) | 12/31/2024 | 12/31/2023 |
|---|---|---|
| Stock options | 680 | 1,697 |
| Unvested RSUs and RSAs | 134,253 | 157,130 |
| **Convertible Notes (if-converted)** | **85,945** | 89,379 |

### How the 85,945 thousand is built (from the Debt note)

| Series | Principal at 12/31/24 | Conversion rate per $1,000 | Max shares (thous.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.25% 2025 Notes | $36.24M | 46.1233 | 1,672 |
| 0.75% 2026 Notes | $249.75M | 43.8481 | 10,951 |
| 0% 2027 Notes | $1,150M | 11.2042 ($89.25/sh) | 12,885 |
| 0.125% 2028 Notes | $1,500M | 17.7494 ($56.34/sh) | 26,624 |
| 0.50% 2030 Notes | $750M | 45.0846 ($22.18/sh) | 33,813 |
| **Total** | **$3.686B** | | **≈85,945** |

Context worth noting:
- That equals roughly **5% of the ~1.69 billion Class A/B/C shares outstanding** at year‑end (1,436.5M A + 22.5M B + 231.6M C).
- Snap reaffirmed in the same filing that **as of 12/31/2024 the if-converted value of the notes did not exceed principal** (all series were out-of-the-money), so none were actually dilutive to reported EPS — the 85,945k is the "maximum" exposure if fully converted into stock.
- Capped call transactions (remaining on the 2026, 2027, 2028 and 2030 Notes; the 2025 capped calls were terminated in May 2024) are intended to offset dilution up to cap prices of $32.58, $121.02, $93.90 and $33.48 respectively, so *economic* dilution would be lower unless the stock trades above those caps.

Sources: Snap Inc. FY2024 Form 10-K (SEC accession 0001564408‑25‑000019), Note “Net Loss per Share” (R54) and Note “Debt” (R15).
judge_reason: The answer's 85,945 thousand / ~85.9 million is a rounding of the official 85,945,127 shares, with no contradiction.
